story_description: Implement the central coordination layer that orchestrates registry fetching, caching, and installation, exposing a unified ObservableObject API for SwiftUI consumption in onboarding and settings screens.
task_description: Create the main orchestrator class that combines RegistryFetcher, RegistryCache, and RegistryInstaller into a cohesive facade, managing async refresh flows, error handling, and published state for UI binding.
atom_description: Implement RegistryCoordinator as an ObservableObject in Blaze/Sources/Registry/RegistryCoordinator.swift that serves as the single entry point for all registry operations. The coordinator exposes @Published properties for skills, plugins, and agents arrays, loading state, error state, and installation progress. It orchestrates the fetch-cache-install pipeline by delegating to RegistryFetcher for network requests, RegistryCache for SQLite persistence with 24h TTL, and RegistryInstaller for file system operations. The coordinator handles automatic cache refresh on launch, manual refresh triggers, background refresh scheduling, and graceful degradation when offline. It provides async methods for loadRegistry(), refreshRegistry(force:), installItem(_:), uninstallItem(_:), and checkForUpdates(). Error handling includes retry logic with exponential backoff, offline mode detection, and user-friendly error message generation.
problem_statement: The Blaze app has separate components for fetching (R002), caching (R003), and installing (R004) registry items, but no unified API to orchestrate these operations. Without a coordinator, UI code would need to manually sequence fetch-cache-install operations, handle errors at multiple levels, and manage complex async state. The coordinator provides a clean ObservableObject facade that encapsulates all registry complexity and exposes simple published properties for SwiftUI binding.

functional_requirements: FR-01: RegistryCoordinator must initialize with injected RegistryFetcher, RegistryCache, and RegistryInstaller dependencies
FR-02: loadRegistry() must first check cache for valid (under 24h TTL) data and return immediately if available
FR-03: loadRegistry() must fetch from network if cache is empty or expired, then update cache
FR-04: loadRegistry() must update @Published skills, plugins, agents arrays on MainActor after successful load
FR-05: loadRegistry() must set @Published error if both cache and network fail
FR-06: refreshRegistry(force: true) must bypass cache and fetch fresh data from network
FR-07: refreshRegistry(force: false) must only fetch if cache TTL expired
FR-08: installItem() must delegate to RegistryInstaller and update installationProgress during operation
FR-09: installItem() must verify item signature before installation via RegistryFetcher
FR-10: uninstallItem() must delegate to RegistryInstaller and update local state
FR-11: checkForUpdates() must compare installed versions against registry versions and return update list
FR-12: isInstalled() must query RegistryInstaller for installation status
FR-13: Coordinator must automatically trigger loadRegistry() on initialization
FR-14: Coordinator must retry failed network requests up to 3 times with exponential backoff
FR-15: Coordinator must detect offline state and set appropriate error message
FR-16: Coordinator must emit Combine notifications for state changes
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-01: Initial load from warm cache must complete in under 50ms
NFR-02: UI must remain responsive during network fetch operations
NFR-03: Memory usage must not exceed 10MB for loaded registry data
NFR-04: Installation progress updates must occur at least every 500ms during active install
NFR-05: Error messages must be user-friendly and actionable
NFR-06: All public methods must have documentation comments
NFR-07: Code must pass SwiftLint with zero violations

edge_cases: Network request times out during loadRegistry() - should retry then fall back to cache
Cache is corrupted or unreadable - should clear cache and fetch fresh
Installation interrupted by app termination - should resume or cleanup on next launch
Multiple concurrent installItem() calls for same item - should deduplicate or queue
refreshRegistry() called while loadRegistry() in progress - should cancel and restart
Device goes offline during installation - should pause and resume when online
Registry response contains items with duplicate IDs - should deduplicate by ID
Cache TTL expires exactly during loadRegistry() - should fetch fresh data
Very large registry response causes memory pressure - should stream parse if needed
User force quits during uninstallItem() - should cleanup partial state on next launch
failure_modes: Network timeout after all retries - set error to networkError, show cached data if available
Invalid JSON in network response - set error to validationError, show cached data
Cache database locked by another process - set error to cacheError, fetch from network
Installation directory not writable - set error to installationError, show permission guidance
Downloaded item fails signature verification - set error to validationError, do not install
Insufficient disk space during installation - set error to installationError, show space needed
Dependency injection receives nil dependencies - assert in debug, provide defaults in release

notes: This coordinator is the central facade for the entire registry subsystem. All UI code interacts with the coordinator rather than individual components. Design decisions here affect UX responsiveness, error handling quality, and testability. The coordinator must balance simplicity of API with flexibility for different usage patterns (onboarding wizard vs settings screen vs background updates).

risks: Coordinator may become too complex if trying to handle too many edge cases inline
Race conditions possible between concurrent loadRegistry() and refreshRegistry() calls
Memory leaks possible if Task references create retain cycles
Offline detection may be unreliable on certain network configurations
Error message quality depends on underlying component error granularity
mitigations: Extract complex logic to private helper methods with single responsibility
Use actor isolation or explicit locking for concurrent state access
Use weak self in Task closures and explicit task cancellation
Supplement NWPathMonitor with actual network request failure detection
Define rich error types in dependencies with context for user-friendly messages
risk_register.blast_radius: Medium - coordinator is central facade so bugs affect all registry UI. However, fallback to cache limits user-facing impact. Individual components (fetcher, cache, installer) remain functional independently.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If coordinator design proves inadequate, UI can temporarily bypass coordinator and call fetcher/cache/installer directly. This is not recommended long-term but provides escape hatch during development.
